chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Zakariyya ibn 'Imran al-Qummi, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from a man among the companions of Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, whose name I did not preserve, who said:
I heard Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام saying:

Indeed, 'Isa ibn Maryam عليه السلام was given two letters by which he used to act, and Musa was given four letters, and Ibrahim was given eight letters, and Nuh was given fifteen letters, and Adam was given twenty-five letters. And indeed Allah, the Exalted, gathered all of that for Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله, and indeed the Greatest Name of Allah consists of seventy-three letters. Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله was given seventy-two letters, and one letter was concealed from him.

key_terms.إِبْرَاهِيمُ: Ibrahim عليه السلام, a prophet given eight letters
key_terms.اثْنَيْنِ وَسَبْعِينَ حَرْفًا: seventy-two letters, the amount given to Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.اسْمَ اللَّهِ الْأَعْظَمَ: the Greatest Name of Allah, whose letters are the subject of the hadith
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةٌ وَسَبْعُونَ حَرْفًا: seventy-three letters, the total number attributed to the Greatest Name
key_terms.حُجِبَ: was concealed or veiled, referring to the one remaining letter
key_terms.عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ: 'Isa son of Maryam عليه السلام, mentioned here as one of the prophets granted part of the Greatest Name
key_terms.مُوسَى: Musa عليه السلام, a prophet given four letters

ai.seo_question: How many letters of the Greatest Name of Allah were given to Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله according to al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the distribution of the letters of the Greatest Name of Allah among the prophets, culminating in their gathering for Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله. It emphasizes the extraordinary divine knowledge granted to him, while affirming that one letter remained veiled.
